chunks: And from his supplications (peace be upon him), in which he seeks refuge with Allah to guide him to the right path.

key_terms.الرُّشَادِ: The right path, sound judgment, or guidance to truth
key_terms.يَلْجَأُ: He seeks refuge or turns to

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-rushad' in Shia supplications?
ai.summary: In this supplication from Nahj al-Balagha, the Imam (peace be upon him) models the spiritual posture of humble reliance on Allah, specifically invoking divine guidance to 'al-rushad,' which Shia scholars interpret as the ultimate state of clarity and sound judgment in both belief and action. This reflects the Shi'a emphasis on the Imam as the perfect exemplar of human potential, demonstrating that even the infallible guide seeks continuous refinement of his connection with the Divine. The act of 'laj'a' (seeking refuge) underscores the necessity of active supplication as a means to attain spiritual rectitude.
